findings.text: cgroupstats_build fills a caller-provided statistics record by counting tasks attached to the hierarchy directory named by a dentry. It rejects dentries that are not directories of the v1 filesystem, resolves the associated hierarchy object under read-side protection with a reference hold, walks all member tasks with the css iterator, releases the reference, and reports success or a negative error.

Task census buckets are exclusive: sampled running, interruptible sleep, uninterruptible sleep and stopped states each increment their own counter, while any other sampled state increments the I/O-wait counter only when the task I/O-wait flag is set.

cgroup1_release_agent is a work-queue handler for hierarchy objects. It exits early when no agent is configured, allocates bounded temporary buffers for agent and path, snapshots the configured agent path under protection, resolves the hierarchy-relative path in the initial namespace, launches the helper synchronously, then releases both buffers.

Release-agent launch uses a two-entry argument list naming the agent binary and the affected hierarchy path plus termination, and a two-entry environment defining home and a standard system search path plus termination, executed with a synchronous execution wait.
cgroup_path_ns provides a thread-safe query that renders the path of a hierarchy object relative to the root visible in a given namespace into a caller buffer and returns status.
The locked path helper first maps the target namespace root set plus hierarchy root to the visible hierarchy root, then builds a relative kernfs path between the target node and that root node.
Path construction holds the outer hierarchy mutex and the inner css-set lock in interrupt-disabled mode across the locked computation, releasing in reverse order.

call_usermodehelper is a convenience that selects an atomic allocation mode for detached launches and a sleeping mode otherwise, allocates a helper descriptor from path plus argument and environment vectors, executes it, and reports allocation failure as out-of-memory.

call_usermodehelper_setup allocates a zeroed helper descriptor, attaches the execution work item, records path plus argument and environment references with optional initialization, cleanup and private data hooks, honoring a static-path build override when present, and returns null on allocation failure.

call_usermodehelper_exec validates the descriptor path, serializes against a global disable flag, treats an empty path as a successful no-op, otherwise publishes a completion object only when a waiter exists, queues the work on the default queue, and implements detached versus waiting behavior with freezable and killable modifiers.

Helper wait progresses from queued to completed: detached mode returns immediately with ownership transferred to the worker; waiting modes block uninterruptibly unless freezable or killable modifiers apply; a kill-interrupted waiter atomically detaches its completion and falls back to an uninterruptible wait; the final status is taken from the descriptor result field.

Helper descriptor lifetime ends exactly once: the waiter releases after harvesting the result, or the completion path releases when detached; an optional cleanup hook runs before release; missing path is an invalid-argument error and launch while disabled is a busy error.

Helper serialization uses a running-helper counter incremented on entry with an ordering barrier and decremented on exit, waking waiters when the last helper finishes; the count is held across disable check, queueing and waiting.

cgroup1_rename is a kernfs rename hook that rejects names containing a newline, rejects non-directory nodes and cross-parent moves, temporarily drops kernfs active protection before acquiring the hierarchy mutex, performs the rename with path tracing on success, then restores protection.

Option display enumerates enabled controllers by legacy name, appends boolean hierarchy flags, shows the release-agent setting only when non-empty under its spin protection, and appends clone-children and named-hierarchy indicators when set.
cgroup_root_from_kf derives the hierarchy descriptor by interpreting the kernfs root node private pointer as the root hierarchy object and returning its hierarchy link.

Version-one mount parsing accepts a fixed flag and string table, falls back to filesystem-source parsing for unmatched keys, then matches legacy controller names while rejecting absent or disabled controllers and accumulating an enable mask, rejecting unknown keys.

Agent and name options each forbid double specification; agent setup requires the initial user namespace and administrative capability; names must be non-empty, length-bounded, limited to alphanumerics plus dot dash underscore, and rejected when named hierarchies are disabled by boot policy.

Option consistency intersects the requested mask with actually available controllers, defaults an otherwise empty specification to all controllers, forbids combining all with explicit names, requires a mask or a name, restricts no-prefix to cpuset-only mounts, and forbids combining none with any mask.

Reconfiguration validates options under offline-drained hierarchy lock, warns about deprecated option changes, computes added and removed controller sets, forbids flag or name changes and refuses populated hierarchies as busy, rebinds controllers, updates the agent path under its lock, and traces the remount.

rebind_subsystems moves a mask of controllers to a destination hierarchy under the hierarchy mutex, first validating all members then migrating each controller with hierarchy-mask updates, effective-set relocation, control reapplication and optional bind notification, finally activating the destination node.

Rebinding refuses to move a controller that still has non-root state unless it is implicit on the default hierarchy, and refuses moves directly between two non-default hierarchies; enable failures during migration are reported as warnings rather than aborting the whole operation.

During relocation the css-set interrupt-disabled lock is held while effective sets are moved between hierarchies in order and in-flight task iterators whose head pointed at the source list are repointed at the destination list to preserve iteration.

Default-hierarchy control application proceeds in order: propagate enable limits down the subtree, create missing per-hierarchy state objects and populate visible directories, then migrate tasks so associations reflect the new effective state.

Task migration for control changes collects source sets from live descendants excluding the target itself, skips the global thread-group lock when no source has tasks, prepares a self destination on the default hierarchy, adds every task from each source set, executes the move, then finalizes.

Effective control for non-root objects inherits the parent enable set, further restricted to threaded-capable controllers when threaded; root objects use the hierarchy enable mask, further excluding inhibited and implicit controllers on the default hierarchy.

Subtree enable computation starts from requested enables plus implicit controllers, repeatedly adds declared dependencies and intersects with controllers available in the hierarchy, iterating until the set no longer grows.

Enabling walks live descendants and every controller present in each object mask, creates missing state objects with allocation errors propagated, warns if a state object is already being torn down, and propagates directory-population errors.
Version-one mount vocabulary includes flags all, clone_children, cpuset_v2_mode, none, noprefix, xattr, favordynmods and nofavordynmods plus strings name and release_agent.
Release-agent environment uses HOME=/ and PATH=/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin.

Observable helper descriptor carries path, argument vector and environment vector references, a completion pointer that is null when detached, a wait-mode field, a result field, a queued work item, plus optional initialization and cleanup hooks with private data.
Observable statistics record carries separate tallies for running, sleeping, uninterruptible, stopped and I/O-wait tasks, each incremented at most once per visited task during the walk.
The release-agent path string is guarded by a dedicated spinlock across snapshot for execution, display for mount options, and update during remount.
Rename nests locks by breaking kernfs active protection on both nodes before acquiring the hierarchy mutex and restoring protection afterwards, because the mutex ranks outside kernfs references.

Statistics collection can fail with invalid argument for wrong filesystem or non-directory nodes and with missing entry when the hierarchy reference has expired; release-agent launch can silently skip on empty configuration or allocation failure and must release any partially allocated buffers.
